old_caption: The video presents a close-up view of several faceted gemstones, including a prominent blue stone and a smaller, lighter-colored stone, arranged on a bright, reflective surface. The camera slowly rotates around the central stones, shifting perspective to reveal their cut and the way they catch light, creating bright sparkles on their facets. Other gemstones, including a pinkish-red one, are visible in the background, softly blurred. The lighting is bright and even, enhancing the clarity and brilliance of the stones. The overall composition emphasizes the intricate details and reflective quality of the gemstones, with no characters or animals present.
original_wisa_caption: The video showcases a series of close-up shots featuring various gemstones, primarily diamonds, set against a soft, light blue background. The camera pans around the gems, highlighting their intricate facets and vibrant colors. Initially, the focus is on a large, round blue diamond, which is prominently displayed at the center of the frame. As the camera moves, it reveals additional gemstones, including a pink diamond and a clear diamond, each with its own unique cut and sparkle. The lighting is bright and even, emphasizing the brilliance and clarity of the stones. The camera continues to rotate, offering different angles and perspectives of the gemstones, allowing viewers to appreciate their detailed craftsmanship and the way they reflect light. The overall effect is one of elegance and luxury, with the gemstones appearing almost ethereal due to the soft lighting and the smooth, reflective surface they rest upon. There are no characters or animals present; the entire focus remains on the beauty and intricacy of the gemstones.
caption: The video showcases a tight close-up of several faceted, translucent gemstones resting on a bright, glossy white surface under high-key lighting. A pale lavender-white oval brilliant sits at the left, a round blue brilliant at center-right, a pink marquise-cut stone near the top, a red stone along the upper edge, and a large out-of-focus blue gem filling the right background. Throughout the excerpt the cluster re-orients, consistent with an orbiting viewpoint that shifts the relative sizes and positions of the stones. The pale oval brilliant drifts from the left toward the center, turning to present its radiating table-facet pattern more face-on, while the round blue brilliant holds its center-right position as its internal dark facet region shifts. The pink marquise slides from top-center toward the upper-left and the red stone moves toward top-right, altering the background arrangement. The two foreground gems draw gradually closer together horizontally. Star-shaped specular flashes appear, fade, and relocate across the blue and pale facets. The background stones remain softly defocused and the bright reflective ground persists, the motion continuing without a visible cut or settled end.

This is a TEMPORALLY CROPPED EXCERPT from a longer video, not a complete event or a loop.
The first view may already be mid-action; the last view need not contain completion. Different
endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.
Do not shorten a rich caption into a terse technical checklist. Avoid annotation phrases such as
'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.

"problem":"concrete visual mismatch or unsupported assertion"}], "caption":"complete final caption",
"length_note":"empty unless required"}. Keep means unchanged caption and no issues. An edit
must actually correct the cited issue. This is a fallible automatic review, not proof of correctness.
